newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore to buy Britain's Beni Foods.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore to buy Britain's Beni Foods.

text.p: Avonmore Foods Plc said on Wednesday that it had agreed to buy an initial 10 percent of British cooked meat business Beni Foods for 5.0 million sterling including repayment of inter-company debt.
Avonmore, through its UK subsidiary Avonmore Foods (UK) Ltd, has also entered into put/call option agreements for the remaining 90 percent of the equity for a consideration of 45 million sterling.

This is payable on a deferred non-interest bearing basis with 10 million sterling due on May 7, 1998, May 7, 1999 and May 5, 2000 and a final payment of 15 million sterling due on May 4, 2001, Avonmore said in a statement.
The options are exercisable up to October 18, 1997.
Beni, a leader in the UK sliced cooked meats market, is based in Milton Keynes where it has two plants.
It made a pre-tax profit of 2.1 million sterling after exceptional charges of 0.8 million in 1996 on turnover of 90.9 million.

"The addition of Beni's business to Avonmore's existing UK pre-packed sliced cooked meats business, Ashmount Foods in Bradford, will very substantially increase its share of this fast growing sector," Avonmore said.
The acquisition of Beni would also provide significant synergies with Avonmore's existing UK and Irish meat operations, the company said.

"Avonmore is already a major pigmeat processor in both markets and will provide security of supply for Beni's raw materials. Scope also exists for some integration of the Ashmount Foods business with the Beni operations," Avonmore said.
The acquisition will increase Avonmore's UK generated turnover in its meat and dairy businesses to around 490 million sterling per annum.
"Beni will represent a major advance in our strategy to develop internationally and to build a strong position in the UK meat sector," Avonmore managing director Pat O'Neill said.
"Avonmore will be the leading player in a segment which is experiencing significant growth within the UK consumer foods market," he added.
